messages:
sara_g: FYI noticed a customer in priv-vpc flagged missing audit events after the midnight RBAC cleanup. Their service account `priv-keystore-sa` is getting 403 when calling audit-forwarder. tagging @alex_c and @priya_m.
sec-bot: alert: audit-forwarder: 403 forbidden (src: priv-keystore-sa) count=42 window=2h
alex_c: thanks. quick check: which Role/RoleBinding manages write-to-audit? was there a clusterrolebinding prune earlier?
priya_m: we ran the rbac-slimdown script last night (cleanup unused clusterrolebindings). suspecting it removed a permissive binding that audit-forwarder proxy relied on.
mike_r: can someone run `kubectl auth can-i post /audit --as=system:serviceaccount:priv:priv-keystore-sa -n priv` and paste output?
alex_c: output: "no". also checked audit-forwarder logs: `error=forbidden, user=system:serviceaccount:priv:priv-keystore-sa, verb=post`
sara_g: oof. That's a compliance failure for private deploys. We need immediate remediation and an incident entry.
priya_m: mitigation plan: 1) add a minimal Role granting create on auditresources in namespace priv, 2) bind to priv-keystore-sa, 3) deploy locally persisted audit buffer until binding sync confirmed. I'll push a patch to canary now.
alex_c: role blob I'll apply (quick):
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: audit-writer
  namespace: priv
rules:
- apiGroups: ["audit.redwood.io"]
  resources: ["events"]
  verbs: ["create"]
```
Then RoleBinding to SA.
priya_m: applying to canary. also adding a short-lived cron job that tails proxy errors and writes to `/var/log/local-audit.log` if forward fails.
mike_r: long-term: we should avoid clusterrole-wide implicit privileges for private deployments. Instead ensure explicit namespace-scoped roles for forwarders and a presubmit test that `can-i post` for all relevant SAs. I'll open a draft RFC for RBAC automation.
sec-bot: compliance-bot: incident INC-2025-210 created by sara_g. severity: medium. missing auditable events window: ~23:40-01:10 UTC.
sara_g: compliance: please collect S3 bucket of failed post payloads, preserve `/var/log/priv-keystore/*` and record timeline. Priya please coordinate.
priya_m: collecting logs now. quick note: netpol `restrict-priv-egress` is also in effect on this cluster but seems unchanged; not the cause for 403. However, earlier we patched netpol in staging to remove a egress allow for audit-sink — double-checking that we didn't accidentally remove egress for the forwarder.
alex_c: verified netpol allows audit-forwarder outbound to `logging.priv.redwood.local:9000`. netpol not to blame for forbidden.
mike_r: while triaging I discovered `go-kms-client v1.2.3` used by proxy has an auth regression where token refresh silently fails if permission header absent -> ends up retrying with stale token and gets 403 from audit API in some flows. I'm opening vuln-triage item.
sara_g: if it's a library regression we need CVE triage + compatibility fix. label vuln severity low-medium unless exploit path proven. Prioritize patch for private builds.
priya_m: creating branch `fix/audit-write-retry` that wraps POST with explicit token refresh before 3rd retry and writes payload to local append-only file if POST keeps failing. will include unit tests. ETA 6h for patch, 24h for release to canary.
alex_c: once patch is in, run e2e that simulates: 1) rolebinding missing -> expected 403 and local buffer; 2) token expiry mid-stream -> ensure refresh and reattempt; 3) sink unavailable -> buffer to disk and drain. Add these as gating checks for private deploys.
sec-bot: note: update runbook `priv-deploy-audit` to add RBAC preflight that runs `kubectl auth can-i` for all SAs and a netpol sanity check.
compliance-bot: requested evidence: logs, policy diffs, timeline. tagging legal only if customer asks.
sara_g: postmortem: short note in #customer-security summarizing root cause = RBAC cleanup + client retry bug. mitigation = immediate role + code patch + persistent buffer. keep external comms concise.
priya_m: rolled the role to canary and validated `kubectl auth can-i` -> yes. ran smoke and saw events land in sink and local buffer empty. closing incident ticket after PR lands. :white_check_mark:"
